```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 12
    n_vehicles = 4
    Q = 58  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[89, 71], [30, 65], [74, 27], [21, 78], [52, 58], [46, 87], [68, 69], [13, 64], [19, 17], [16, 38], [12, 81], [84, 6]]
    demands = [13, 14, 21, 17, 5, 22, 7, 9, 6, 19, 14, 9]
    time_windows = [[0, 313], [69, 132], [28, 123], [52, 132], [43, 103], [7, 73], [53, 139], [35, 99], [40, 131], [46, 122], [41, 110], [47, 141], [62, 143]]
    service_times = [10, 12, 10, 6, 15, 5, 9, 6, 5, 9, 11, 7]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Vehicle routing and scheduling with time windows and capacity constraints

Overview
We operate a centralized delivery model using a fleet of identical vehicles dispatched from a single depot. The upcoming planning horizon requires us to design out-and-back routes so that each customer is served once within their agreed delivery window, while ensuring vehicles return to the depot before the depot’s latest closing time. The routing plan must balance service commitments with operating cost and fleet utilization.

Routing and scheduling challenge
- All vehicles will depart the depot at time 0 and complete exactly one trip each. Each trip consists of leaving the depot, visiting a sequence of assigned customers, and returning to the depot before the depot’s closing time.
- Every customer must be visited exactly once. Deliveries cannot be split across vehicles, and there are no mid-route returns or transfers.
- Travel time between any two locations is based on straight-line distance between their coordinates under unit speed (one unit of distance equals one unit of travel time).

Service and timing requirements
- Each customer has a delivery time window with an earliest and latest acceptable start time. Service must begin within this window.
- If a vehicle arrives early, it must wait until the window opens. After service begins, the vehicle remains on site for the specified service/unloading time and departs immediately upon completion.
- Vehicles must complete all visits and return to the depot before the depot’s latest time for the planning horizon.

Capacity constraints
- Each vehicle has a fixed carrying capacity. The total assigned demand on a vehicle’s route must not exceed this capacity at any point during the route.
- No split deliveries are permitted; demand for a customer must be fulfilled by a single vehicle during its single visit.

Cost structure
- Each vehicle used incurs a fixed deployment cost in addition to distance-based travel cost. We may choose to deploy fewer than the maximum available vehicles if feasible.
- The planning objective is to serve all customers exactly once, meet all time window and capacity constraints, and minimize the sum of total travel distance and vehicle deployment costs.

Expected outcome
The required output is a set of feasible routes and detailed stop schedules for the available fleet that:
- Satisfy all customer time windows (with waiting when early),
- Respect service times at each stop and vehicle capacity limits,
- Ensure every vehicle departs at time 0 and returns before the depot’s closing time,
- Minimize total cost (travel distance plus fixed deployment costs).
